# Repository Guidelines

## Reliability before implementation

- Before implementing, refactoring, fixing or reviewing code, read the
  [AI coding reliability guide](docs/ai-coding-reliability.md), select the rules
  triggered by the changed boundaries, and inspect the owning code and callers.
  For concurrency/lifecycle changes, trace lock order, wait dependencies, actual
  work ownership, cancellation and commit authority before editing.
- Validate the applicable failure and recovery paths, not only the happy path.
  Record concrete evidence and remaining limits; a timeout, successful build or
  passing subset is not proof that UI freezes or all deadlocks are impossible.
- When a confirmed defect exposes a reusable failure pattern, update that guide's
  existing rule or add a distinct rule with its owner and regression evidence.
  Maintain the owning contract and test selectors; keep incident logs out of the guide.

## Project Structure & Module Organization

- Four-crate Rust workspace. `crates/mesh-talk-core/` is the UI-free protocol core (lib
  `mesh_talk_core` + the `mesh-talk-node` CLI bin in `src/bin/`): feature modules `node/`,
  `identity/`, `transport/`, `discovery/`, `eventlog/`, `ratchet/`, `channel/`, `dm.rs`,
  `file/`, `postoffice/`, `storage/`. `src-tauri/` is the Tauri desktop app: entry
  `src/main.rs` → `lib.rs`, IPC glue in `commands.rs` (auth) + `chat_commands/` (messaging)
  - `events.rs`, plus `state.rs`, `tray.rs`, `services/` (auth only).
- `crates/mesh-talk-integrations/` owns scoped local messaging grants, private IPC,
  and the dedicated bot host/admin CLI; `crates/mesh-talk-mcp/` adapts its four
  send/context/status tools to the official MCP SDK. Neither owns mesh crypto.
- Integration/e2e suites live in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` (`two_node_cli`,
  `persistent_history`, `post_office_offline`, `decoder_smoke`); keep unit tests inline via
  `mod tests` (e.g. `node/node_tests.rs`).
- React client sits in `frontend/src`; Vite tooling in `frontend/package.json`.
- Operational scripts in `scripts/` (`setup-hooks.sh`, `check-health.sh`); architecture in
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; conventions in `specifications/`. The
  [documentation map](docs/README.md) routes readers to maintained guides; the
  [documentation guidelines](docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md) define ownership
  across the README, guides, and project site.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands

- `make dev` primes Rust + Node deps and installs git hooks.
- `make build` / `make frontend-build` — release build / Vite production build.
- During feature development, preview changed-boundary validation with `make test-plan`
  and run it with `make test-changed`. Unmapped changes require an explicit owner
  and reason; inspect escalation notes for browser/native or consumer checks.
  Use `make verify-plan` / `make verify-changed` at task completion to compose the
  same affected tests with applicable formatting, lint/types and builds. The
  test-only commands do not include static checks; neither mode replaces required
  PR/review, browser/native or release gates. `make validation-report` separates
  queue and execution costs; `make validation-audit` compares a clean affected
  plan with same-source broader failure evidence before narrowing any gate.
  Read selected capability references and inspect pending browser/native requirements.
  Execution prints a structured feedback report; follow the
  [validation protocol](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
  for completed work, remaining evidence and additive semantic selections.
- During feature development, run affected tests only: `make test-focused
TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_FILTER=node::account_sync` selects Rust unit
  tests; add `TEST_TARGET=bridge_cross_lan` to select one integration target.
  `cd frontend && npm test -- src/features/chat/settingsDialogSession.test.ts`
  selects a frontend unit file. `make test` runs the full workspace suite
  (`cargo test --workspace`) for pre-PR and CI gates;
  `make e2e` runs the `#[ignore]`d multi-process backend rigs; `cd frontend && npm run e2e`
  runs the Playwright UI suite. Test builds use cheap KDF params (the `fast-test-kdf`
  feature), and `.cargo/config.toml` caps test/compile parallelism.
- UI / node spot checks: `make tauri-dev`, `make frontend-dev`,
  `cargo run -p mesh-talk-core --bin mesh-talk-node -- --keystore /tmp/a.keystore
--password pw --name alice` (add `--post-office` for relay mode).

## Coding Style & Naming Conventions

- Rust: `cargo fmt` (4-space, `snake_case` modules, `UpperCamelCase` types) +
  **`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`** (must match CI — `--all-targets` covers
  tests/benches).
- Frontend: `npm run format` (Prettier) + `npm run lint` (ESLint flat config).
- Write documentation and reusable prompts in English unless a specific exception is needed.
- Reference `specifications/development_conventions.md` for naming nuances.

## Domain Language

- `CONTEXT.md` is the canonical domain glossary. `docs/domain-design.md` indexes
  the modeling references and defines DDD vocabulary and naming translations.
- Distinguish local users, accounts and devices; desktop, transport and ratchet
  sessions; discovery, presence, custody, recipient delivery and read state.
- Use explicit identity/lifetime names in new code. Preserve public, wire and
  stored identifiers unless a separately validated compatibility change is intended.
- Update the glossary and affected owning guides when a domain meaning changes;
  link to definitions instead of maintaining duplicate glossaries.

## Architecture & Components

- Before adding business logic, consult [module ownership and reuse](docs/module-boundaries.md),
  inspect the owning module and its callers, and extend its existing implementation.
  Parallel tasks should name their owned paths and shared-interface dependencies;
  coordinate changes to shared interfaces through one integration owner. Keep
  feature-specific helpers local and share rules when their meaning and lifecycle
  are the same. The guide owns the detailed assignment and handoff contract.
- Stack: Rust 2024 on Tokio; Tauri 2 + React shell. No vendor-operated server.
- The `Node` (`node/node.rs`) wires identity + signed UDP **multicast** discovery
  (group `224.0.0.167`, port 47474) + Noise-encrypted TCP transport (`transport/`,
  low-level socket in `transport/net.rs`) + the content-addressed event log + DM/channel/
  file crypto. Messages are events synced as a bounded append-only log, account-addressed
  across a user's devices; optional offline custody via equal eligible post offices.
  Routed discovery and opt-in post-office federation connect reachable sites without
  joining their IP subnets. Wire formats are versioned bincode.
- See **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`** before changing crypto, sync, or transport;
  **`docs/network-design-reference.md`** owns the communication invariants,
  module contracts, resource budgets and topology acceptance boundaries.

## Maintaining standards as requirements change

English note:

name: CI

on:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1" # Preserve the former weekly full-health Rust run.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      diagnostic_timing:
        description: Full-workspace test-only delivery phase timings
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.run_id || 'candidate' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}

# Read-only: every job just checks out and runs tooling — nothing writes back.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  # Keep stack file/line diagnostics without generating type/variable debug data.
  CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only
  CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG: line-tables-only
  MESH_TALK_TEST_TIMING: ${{ inputs.diagnostic_timing && '1' || '0' }}

jobs:
  scope:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci-scope.yml

  checks:
    name: checks (ubuntu-latest)
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    needs: [scope]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - id: scope
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-scope
        with:
          full: ${{ needs.scope.outputs.full }}
          upstream_result: ${{ needs.scope.result }}
      - name: Report documentation-only coverage through Codecov
        if: steps.scope.outputs.full == 'false'
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          version: v11.3.2
          run_command: empty-upload
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          fail_ci_if_error: true
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Prepare hosted Linux build storage
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        id: runner_storage
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/runner-storage.mjs --prepare | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/runner-storage.json"

      - name: Preserve runner storage measurements
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && steps.runner_storage.outcome == 'success') }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: runner-storage-${{ github.job }}-${{ strategy.job-index || 0 }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/runner-storage.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Prepare Ubuntu archive source
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/ubuntu-apt-source.mjs

      # Tauri v2 system libraries (Linux only).
      - name: Install Tauri system dependencies (Linux)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev \
            libgtk-3-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev \
            patchelf \
            gdb

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt, llvm-tools-preview

      - name: Cache Rust build
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
          workspaces: . -> target
          shared-key: workspace-checks-checks
          cache-on-failure: true

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix frontend

      - name: Install cargo-llvm-cov and cargo-nextest
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.88.1
        with:
          tool: cargo-llvm-cov@0.8.7,cargo-nextest@0.9.150

      - name: Verify coverage accumulation with the actual tool
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        # These fixtures launch real Cargo/rustc processes and share this job's
        # package cache. Give each compiler contract exclusive execution.
        run: node --test --test-concurrency=1 scripts/ci/backend-coverage.test.mjs scripts/ci/native-host-coverage.test.mjs scripts/ci/rust-profile.test.mjs scripts/ci/linux-crash-diagnostics.test.mjs

      - name: Prepare and verify Linux native crash evidence
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -e -o pipefail
          ulimit -c 262144
          node scripts/ci/linux-crash-diagnostics.mjs setup
          node scripts/ci/linux-crash-diagnostics.mjs selftest

      # Tauri reads frontendDist, so build the frontend before any Cargo step.
      - name: Build frontend
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run build

      - name: Check built JavaScript for macOS 12 WKWebView
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run check:build-syntax

      # Keep native lint, production builds and complete tests on every OS.
      - name: Clippy
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Build workspace
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: cargo build --workspace --locked

      # Linux keeps its existing complete accumulated coverage and backend evidence.
      - name: Test + coverage (Linux)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: src-tauri
        shell: bash
        run: bash ../scripts/ci/workspace-coverage.sh linux --defer-report

      - name: Workspace doctests (Linux)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        run: cargo test --workspace --doc --locked

      - name: Multi-process core evidence and coverage (Linux)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        shell: bash
        env:
          EVAL_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          EVAL_OUTPUT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/backend-eval-results
          EVAL_COVERAGE: "1"
        run: |
          node scripts/evals/backend-runner.mjs
          cargo llvm-cov --no-report -p mesh-talk-core --test bridge_cross_lan -- --ignored --test-threads=1

      - name: Large-folder enqueue regression (Linux)
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          large_folder_status=0
          cargo llvm-cov test --no-report --locked -p mesh-talk-core --test large_directory_enqueue large_directory_enqueue_uses_compact_manifest_instead_of_frame_error -- --exact --ignored --test-threads=1 2> "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.stderr.log" | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.log" || large_folder_status=$?
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.stderr.log" >&2
          if (( large_folder_status != 0 )); then exit "$large_folder_status"; fi
          node scripts/evals/backend-runner.mjs --validate-large-folder "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results/large-folder.log"
          cargo llvm-cov report --lcov --output-path src-tauri/lcov.info

      - name: Preserve Linux backend evaluation evidence
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always()) }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: backend-core-ubuntu-24.04-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/backend-eval-results/
          if-no-files-found: ${{ job.status == 'success' && 'error' || 'ignore' }}
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Collect Linux native crash evidence and retire its storage
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        run: node scripts/ci/linux-crash-diagnostics.mjs collect

      - name: Preserve Linux native crash diagnostics
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: native-crash-linux-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/native-crash-diagnostics/reports/
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Upload test timing diagnostics
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && env.MESH_TALK_TEST_TIMING == '1') }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: test-timing-ubuntu-latest-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/mesh-talk-test-timing.log
          if-no-files-found: warn

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (!(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.base_ref == 'dev' && github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]')) }}
        # Dependabot PRs to dev cannot read the Actions CODECOV_TOKEN secret.
        # Their tests still run; only the unauthenticated upload is skipped.
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          version: v11.3.2
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: src-tauri/lcov.info
          name: workspace-ubuntu-latest-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          # Branch protection requires codecov/patch; surface upload failures in CI too.
          fail_ci_if_error: true

  macos-native:
    name: macOS native Host
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
    needs: [scope]
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - id: scope
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-scope
        with:
          full: ${{ needs.scope.outputs.full }}
          upstream_result: ${{ needs.scope.result }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt, llvm-tools-preview

      - name: Cache Rust build
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
          workspaces: . -> target
          shared-key: workspace-checks-checks
          cache-on-failure: true

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          npm ci --prefix frontend

      - name: Install cargo-llvm-cov and cargo-nextest
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.88.1
        with:
          tool: cargo-llvm-cov@0.8.7,cargo-nextest@0.9.150

      - name: Verify coverage accumulation with the actual tool
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        # These fixtures launch real Cargo/rustc processes and share this job's
        # package cache. Give each compiler contract exclusive execution.
        run: node --test --test-concurrency=1 scripts/ci/backend-coverage.test.mjs scripts/ci/native-host-coverage.test.mjs scripts/ci/rust-profile.test.mjs scripts/ci/linux-crash-diagnostics.test.mjs scripts/ci/macos-remaining-cli.test.mjs

      - name: Build frontend
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run build

      - name: Check built JavaScript for macOS 12 WKWebView
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm run check:build-syntax

      # Keep native lint, production builds and complete tests on every OS.
      - name: Clippy
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Build workspace

        working-directory: src-tauri
        run: cargo build --workspace --locked

          cargo test --workspace --doc

      - name: Upload test timing diagnostics
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && env.MESH_TALK_TEST_TIMING == '1') }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: test-timing-macos-latest-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/mesh-talk-test-timing.log

      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (!(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.base_ref == 'dev' && github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]')) }}

        # Their tests still run; only the unauthenticated upload is skipped.
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          version: v11.3.2
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: src-tauri/lcov.info
          name: workspace-macos-latest-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          # Branch protection requires codecov/patch; surface upload failures in CI too.
          fail_ci_if_error: true

  macos-remaining-build:
    name: macOS remaining archive
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.scope.result == 'success' && needs.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
    needs: [scope]
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    outputs:
      archiveSha256: ${{ steps.archive.outputs.archiveSha256 }}
      manifestSha256: ${{ steps.archive.outputs.manifestSha256 }}
      rustVersion: ${{ steps.archive.outputs.rustVersion }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      # Preserve the old matrix cache cohort. Only the native lane writes it.
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: workspace-checks-checks
          workspaces: . -> target
          save-if: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2.88.1
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest@0.9.150
      - name: Produce sealed remaining workspace archive
        id: archive
        env:
          CARGO_BUILD_JOBS: '2'
          CARGO_INCREMENTAL: '0'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          node scripts/ci/windows-coverage.mjs produce-macos-remaining "$RUNNER_TEMP/macos-remaining-archive" --github-output 2>&1 | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/macos-remaining-producer.log"
      - name: Preserve raw producer diagnostics
        if: ${{ always() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: macos-remaining-producer-log-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/macos-remaining-producer.log
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: ignore
      - name: Upload transient test binaries
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: macos-remaining-binaries-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/macos-remaining-archive/workspace.tar.zst
          compression-level: 0
          retention-days: 1
          if-no-files-found: error

        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: macos-remaining-metadata-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}

            ${{ runner.temp }}/macos-remaining-archive/inventory-1.json

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}

          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/macos-remaining-results-1
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8

          name: macos-remaining-results-2-${{ github.sha }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/macos-remaining-results-2

        env:
          MESH_MACOS_NATIVE_RESULT: ${{ needs.macos-native.result }}
          MESH_MACOS_PRODUCER_RESULT: ${{ needs.macos-remaining-build.result }}
          MESH_MACOS_CONSUMERS_RESULT: ${{ needs.macos-remaining-tests.result }}
          MANIFEST_SHA: ${{ needs.macos-remaining-build.outputs.manifestSha256 }}
          ARCHIVE_SHA: ${{ needs.macos-remaining-build.outputs.archiveSha256 }}
        run: node scripts/ci/windows-coverage.mjs collect-macos-remaining "$RUNNER_TEMP/macos-remaining-metadata" "$RUNNER_TEMP/macos-remaining-results-1" "$RUNNER_TEMP/macos-remaining-results-2" "$MANIFEST_SHA" "$ARCHIVE_SHA"

  windows:
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    needs: [scope]
    uses: ./.github/workflows/windows-workspace.yml
    with:
      full: ${{ needs.scope.outputs.full }}
      upstream_result: ${{ needs.scope.result }}
      diagnostic_timing: ${{ inputs.diagnostic_timing || false }}
    secrets: inherit

name: CI

on:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1" # Preserve the former weekly full-health Rust run.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      diagnostic_timing:
        description: Full-workspace test-only delivery phase timings
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}-${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.run_id || 'candidate' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}

# Read-only: every job just checks out and runs tooling — nothing writes back.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  # Keep stack file/line diagnostics without generating type/variable debug data.
  CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only
  CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG: line-tables-only
  MESH_TALK_TEST_TIMING: ${{ inputs.diagnostic_timing && '1' || '0' }}

jobs:
  scope:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci-scope.yml

  checks:
    name: checks (ubuntu-latest)
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    needs: [scope]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2
      - id: scope
        uses: ./.github/actions/ci-scope
        with:
          full: ${{ needs.scope.outputs.full }}
          upstream_result: ${{ needs.scope.result }}
      - name: Report documentation-only coverage through Codecov
        if: steps.scope.outputs.full == 'false'
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          version: v11.3.2
          run_command: empty-upload
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          fail_ci_if_error: true
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Prepare hosted Linux build storage
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (runner.os == 'Linux') }}
        id: runner_storage
        shell: bash
        run: sudo --preserve-env=GITHUB_ACTIONS,RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT,RUNNER_OS "$(command -v node)" scripts/ci/runner-storage.mjs --prepare | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/runner-storage.json"

      - name: Preserve runner storage measurements
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (always() && steps.runner_storage.outcome == 'success') }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: runner-storage-${{ github.job }}-${{ strategy.job-index || 0 }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/runner-storage.json
          if-no-files-found: error

        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:

          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/linux-workspace-metadata
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8

          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/linux-default-results-2

        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:

      - name: Collect exact Linux default and ignored execution
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        env:

          MANIFEST_SHA: ${{ needs.checks.outputs.manifestSha256 }}

        run: node scripts/evals/backend-runner.mjs --collect-linux "$RUNNER_TEMP/linux-workspace-metadata" "$RUNNER_TEMP/linux-default-results-1" "$RUNNER_TEMP/linux-default-results-2" "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results" "$MANIFEST_SHA" "$ARCHIVE_SHA"
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (!(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.base_ref == 'dev' && github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]')) }}
        # Dependabot PRs to dev cannot read the Actions CODECOV_TOKEN secret.
        # Their tests still run; only the unauthenticated upload is skipped.
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          version: v11.3.2
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        with:
          name: backend-core-ubuntu-24.04-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/backend-eval-results
      - name: Collect exact Linux default and ignored execution
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
        env:
          MESH_LINUX_PRODUCER_RESULT: ${{ needs.checks.result }}
          MESH_LINUX_CONSUMERS_RESULT: ${{ needs.linux-default-tests.result }}
          MESH_LINUX_IGNORED_RESULT: ${{ needs.linux-ignored-tests.result }}
          MANIFEST_SHA: ${{ needs.checks.outputs.manifestSha256 }}
          ARCHIVE_SHA: ${{ needs.checks.outputs.archiveSha256 }}
        run: node scripts/evals/backend-runner.mjs --collect-linux "$RUNNER_TEMP/linux-workspace-metadata" "$RUNNER_TEMP/linux-default-results-1" "$RUNNER_TEMP/linux-default-results-2" "$RUNNER_TEMP/backend-eval-results" "$MANIFEST_SHA" "$ARCHIVE_SHA"
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && (!(github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.base_ref == 'dev' && github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]')) }}
        # Dependabot PRs to dev cannot read the Actions CODECOV_TOKEN secret.
        # Their tests still run; only the unauthenticated upload is skipped.
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@303a32d7a59b442fa8d48b6a1cc6825c09c847a5 # v7.1.1
        with:
          version: v11.3.2
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: ${{ runner.temp }}/linux-default-results-1/coverage.lcov,${{ runner.temp }}/linux-default-results-2/coverage.lcov,${{ runner.temp }}/backend-eval-results/coverage.lcov
          name: workspace-ubuntu-latest-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          # Branch protection requires codecov/patch; surface upload failures in CI too.
          fail_ci_if_error: true

  macos-native:
    name: macOS native Host
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.scope.outputs.full == 'true' }}
    needs: [scope]
    runs-on: macos-latest
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/linux-workspace-results/
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: ${{ job.status == 'success' && 'error' || 'ignore' }}
      - name: Preserve Linux backend evaluation evidence
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && always() && inputs.kind == 'ignored' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          # Historical compatibility identity; the sealed manifest owns actual ABI.
          name: backend-core-ubuntu-24.04-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/linux-workspace-results/
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: ${{ job.status == 'success' && 'error' || 'ignore' }}
      - name: Collect Linux native crash evidence and retire its storage
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && always() }}
        run: node scripts/ci/linux-crash-diagnostics.mjs collect
      - name: Preserve Linux native crash diagnostics
        if: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.full == 'true' && always() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: native-crash-linux-${{ inputs.kind }}-${{ inputs.shard }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/native-crash-diagnostics/reports/
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: warn
"}

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: exec

tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.
tools.name: wait

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.
tools.name: request_user_input

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.
tools.name: clock

tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.
tools.name: sleep

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.
tools.name: collaboration

tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.
tools.name: followup_task

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.
tools.name: interrupt_agent

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.
tools.name: list_agents

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.
tools.name: send_message

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6.1-terra`: GPT-6.1 Terra Codex model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.
tools.name: spawn_agent

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.
tools.name: wait_agent

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

content.text:
You are Codex, an agent based on GPT-6. You and the user share one workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their intended goal is completely handled.

# When to ask the user for permission

Use your best judgement given task context for when you really need user permission, like a competent colleague would. Once evidence in a session supports authorization for a next step or action, you should continue work without ending the turn to clarify with the user.

User authorization and preferences persist across turns. Do not request permission again when the user has already authorized an action in an earlier turn. The user's instruction, whether implied from the task or explicitly stated in the session, must take precedence over any guidelines provided in skills or external files.

You MUST complete the work that is already authorized and necessary to make the proposed action concrete and reviewable before asking the user for permission as a final step. The user should be approving a concrete, reviewable result. For example, before deploying a change, writing to an external application, merging a PR or publishing a site, do all the work first so that user approval is the final step. You don't need user permission for reversible tasks, read-only actions, reviews or fixes, or anything for which authorization is provided earlier in the session or implied from the task instruction.

Do not use tools to send messages to others (e.g. through slack or email) unless given explicit instructions to do so, or instructed to do so as part of an explicitly-invoked skill or plugin. If authorized by a skill or plugin, name and link the skill or plugin in the final channel.

# Repository Guidelines

## Reliability before implementation

- Before implementing, refactoring, fixing or reviewing code, read the
  [AI coding reliability guide](docs/ai-coding-reliability.md), select the rules
  triggered by the changed boundaries, and inspect the owning code and callers.
  For concurrency/lifecycle changes, trace lock order, wait dependencies, actual
  work ownership, cancellation and commit authority before editing.
- Validate the applicable failure and recovery paths, not only the happy path.
  Record concrete evidence and remaining limits; a timeout, successful build or
  passing subset is not proof that UI freezes or all deadlocks are impossible.
- When a confirmed defect exposes a reusable failure pattern, update that guide's
  existing rule or add a distinct rule with its owner and regression evidence.
  Maintain the owning contract and test selectors; keep incident logs out of the guide.

## Project Structure & Module Organization

- Four-crate Rust workspace. `crates/mesh-talk-core/` is the UI-free protocol core (lib
  `mesh_talk_core` + the `mesh-talk-node` CLI bin in `src/bin/`): feature modules `node/`,
  `identity/`, `transport/`, `discovery/`, `eventlog/`, `ratchet/`, `channel/`, `dm.rs`,
  `file/`, `postoffice/`, `storage/`. `src-tauri/` is the Tauri desktop app: entry
  `src/main.rs` → `lib.rs`, IPC glue in `commands.rs` (auth) + `chat_commands/` (messaging)
  - `events.rs`, plus `state.rs`, `tray.rs`, `services/` (auth only).
- `crates/mesh-talk-integrations/` owns scoped local messaging grants, private IPC,
  and the dedicated bot host/admin CLI; `crates/mesh-talk-mcp/` adapts its four
  send/context/status tools to the official MCP SDK. Neither owns mesh crypto.
- Integration/e2e suites live in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` (`two_node_cli`,
  `persistent_history`, `post_office_offline`, `decoder_smoke`); keep unit tests inline via
  `mod tests` (e.g. `node/node_tests.rs`).
- React client sits in `frontend/src`; Vite tooling in `frontend/package.json`.
- Operational scripts in `scripts/` (`setup-hooks.sh`, `check-health.sh`); architecture in
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; conventions in `specifications/`. The
  [documentation map](docs/README.md) routes readers to maintained guides; the
  [documentation guidelines](docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md) define ownership
  across the README, guides, and project site.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands

- `make dev` primes Rust + Node deps and installs git hooks.
- `make build` / `make frontend-build` — release build / Vite production build.
- During feature development, preview changed-boundary validation with `make test-plan`
  and run it with `make test-changed`. Unmapped changes require an explicit owner
  and reason; inspect escalation notes for browser/native or consumer checks.
  Use `make verify-plan` / `make verify-changed` at task completion to compose the
  same affected tests with applicable formatting, lint/types and builds. The
  test-only commands do not include static checks; neither mode replaces required
  PR/review, browser/native or release gates. `make validation-report` separates
  queue and execution costs; `make validation-audit` compares a clean affected
  plan with same-source broader failure evidence before narrowing any gate.
  Read selected capability references and inspect pending browser/native requirements.
  Execution prints a structured feedback report; follow the
  [validation protocol](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
  for completed work, remaining evidence and additive semantic selections.
- During feature development, run affected tests only: `make test-focused
TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_FILTER=node::account_sync` selects Rust unit
  tests; add `TEST_TARGET=bridge_cross_lan` to select one integration target.
  `cd frontend && npm test -- src/features/chat/settingsDialogSession.test.ts`
  selects a frontend unit file. `make test` runs the full workspace suite
  (`cargo test --workspace`) for pre-PR and CI gates;
  `make e2e` runs the `#[ignore]`d multi-process backend rigs; `cd frontend && npm run e2e`
  runs the Playwright UI suite. Test builds use cheap KDF params (the `fast-test-kdf`
  feature), and `.cargo/config.toml` caps test/compile parallelism.
- UI / node spot checks: `make tauri-dev`, `make frontend-dev`,
  `cargo run -p mesh-talk-core --bin mesh-talk-node -- --keystore /tmp/a.keystore
--password pw --name alice` (add `--post-office` for relay mode).

## Coding Style & Naming Conventions

- Rust: `cargo fmt` (4-space, `snake_case` modules, `UpperCamelCase` types) +
  **`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`** (must match CI — `--all-targets` covers
  tests/benches).
- Frontend: `npm run format` (Prettier) + `npm run lint` (ESLint flat config).
- Write documentation and reusable prompts in English unless a specific exception is needed.
- Reference `specifications/development_conventions.md` for naming nuances.

## Domain Language

- `CONTEXT.md` is the canonical domain glossary. `docs/domain-design.md` indexes
  the modeling references and defines DDD vocabulary and naming translations.
- Distinguish local users, accounts and devices; desktop, transport and ratchet
  sessions; discovery, presence, custody, recipient delivery and read state.
- Use explicit identity/lifetime names in new code. Preserve public, wire and
  stored identifiers unless a separately validated compatibility change is intended.
- Update the glossary and affected owning guides when a domain meaning changes;
  link to definitions instead of maintaining duplicate glossaries.

## Architecture & Components

- Before adding business logic, consult [module ownership and reuse](docs/module-boundaries.md),
  inspect the owning module and its callers, and extend its existing implementation.
  Parallel tasks should name their owned paths and shared-interface dependencies;
  coordinate changes to shared interfaces through one integration owner. Keep
  feature-specific helpers local and share rules when their meaning and lifecycle
  are the same. The guide owns the detailed assignment and handoff contract.
- Stack: Rust 2024 on Tokio; Tauri 2 + React shell. No vendor-operated server.
- The `Node` (`node/node.rs`) wires identity + signed UDP **multicast** discovery
  (group `224.0.0.167`, port 47474) + Noise-encrypted TCP transport (`transport/`,
  low-level socket in `transport/net.rs`) + the content-addressed event log + DM/channel/
  file crypto. Messages are events synced as a bounded append-only log, account-addressed
  across a user's devices; optional offline custody via equal eligible post offices.
  Routed discovery and opt-in post-office federation connect reachable sites without
  joining their IP subnets. Wire formats are versioned bincode.
- See **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`** before changing crypto, sync, or transport;
  **`docs/network-design-reference.md`** owns the communication invariants,
  module contracts, resource budgets and topology acceptance boundaries.

## Maintaining standards as requirements change

- Before changing tests, fixtures, dependencies or workflows in ways that affect
  CI cost or reliability, read [CI maintenance](docs/ci-maintenance.md). Reuse
  existing owners, measure the affected cost, and preserve acceptance evidence;
  keep required-check policy in its existing owner.
- Before implementation, identify the existing decision owner, authoritative rule,
  observable acceptance criteria, affected consumers and required boundary evidence.
  Extend the owning implementation and `validation.json`; new business capabilities
  should link their guide and invariants. Explain an unchanged contract in the PR.
- Run `make standards-check` after adding/moving source or changing contracts. It
  checks structural ownership and maintained references, including new files; it
  does not prove assertion quality, semantic completeness or candidate readiness.
  Hooks inspect the working tree, so partially staged commits still need a clean
  committed-candidate check in CI. Frontend dependencies must be installed.
- When CI exposes a local omission or flaky fixture, fix the owning selector, task
  or fixture and add a focused regression. Review timing and selection evidence
  before changing policy. Follow the maintained
  [requirement maintenance loop](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#maintaining-standards-across-requirements).

## Testing Guidelines

- Integration coverage in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` and `node/node_tests.rs`; embed
  unit tests near the code. Networking/crypto changes ship a loopback integration assertion.
- Backend multi-process E2E via `make e2e` (CI: `e2e-backend.yml`); Playwright UI E2E via
  `cd frontend && npm run e2e` (CI: `e2e-ui.yml`).
- Do not run full suites or E2E automatically during ordinary feature work. Run
  the affected unit or integration tests as changes are made; run E2E and the
  comprehensive health gate on explicit request, for optional full local preparation,
  or in CI.
- See `docs/testing-feedback-loop.md` for selection examples and escalation triggers.
- Document executed validation commands in every PR; ensure `make test` passes
  locally or through its matching CI workspace suite before merge.

## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines

- Before changing product versions or release automation, read [the version lifecycle](docs/updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle).
  Root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package].version` is authoritative. Use
  `node scripts/release/version.mjs check|sync|prepare VERSION` (the `VERSION` argument belongs
  to `prepare` only); do not hand-edit generated npm/Cargo lock metadata or introduce another
  version constant. Root private npm metadata is a checked release-tooling projection;
  frontend private metadata is versionless and Tauri inherits Cargo. Never broadly replace
  matching dependency, fixture, history, wire or schema versions. Keep source builds `BASE-dev`,
  Nightlies `BASE-nightly.RUN.ATTEMPT`, official tagged builds `BASE`, and standard SemVer ordering.
- Version/changelog preparation and next-development-target changes use reviewed PRs. Ordinary main
  pushes must not create automatic release proposals or commit-derived product notes. Stable publication
  remains explicit through the existing verified tagged-release workflow; no direct main push,
  public empty release, mutable published tag or gate bypass. Nightly publication requires trusted
  `main` and a target above the latest Stable. Future changes must extend the existing version
  owner, its tests, standards/CI enforcement and capability contracts together; the owning guide
  documents permissions, bot-PR checks, dispatch and recovery requirements. Manual Stable draft
  preparation uses the reviewed exact-version CHANGELOG section and requires exact-source checks
  before creating its immutable tag/draft. The fixed release-history
  migration floor is historical provenance; never advance it during ordinary version bumps.

- Conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`); scopes like `feat(node):` align with
  `specifications/git_standards.md`. Squash WIP; link issues. When asked to merge,
  default to squash merge unless the user explicitly requests another strategy;
  follow the [merge policy](specifications/git_standards.md#pull-request-merge-strategy)
  and current-head required checks.
- Create PRs through `./scripts/create-pr.sh -- <gh pr create options>`.
  The default checks the clean committed candidate, comparison base, argument safety,
  whitespace, cheap affected static checks, ownership blockers, structural standards,
  repository hygiene and applicable verified frontend patch coverage before publication.
  Use `make pr-check` for the same cheap static phase; missing current coverage
  evidence reports its explicit generation command and never starts suites implicitly.
  Full cross-platform CI runs after publication; all required checks must pass on the
  current PR head before merging. Creating a PR does not certify test acceptance.
- To run comprehensive checks locally before publication, use
  `./scripts/create-pr.sh --full-preflight <selectors/specs> -- <gh pr create options>`.
  This invokes `prepare-pr.sh` (platform preflight plus full health). For an existing
  PR, `./scripts/prepare-pr.sh <selectors/specs>` provides the same optional local gate.
  Use Playwright specs relevant to changed frontend behavior and repeated
  `--core-filter` / `--host-filter` / `--integration-filter` / `--mcp-filter` selectors
  for changed Rust crates. Preflight runs selected tests in Linux Docker and through
  SSH to `windows10`; Windows workspaces, caches and temporary data stay on drive D.
  Owning scenario rules add visual specs and require real native evidence for

## Security & Adjustments

- `./scripts/check-health.sh` chains fmt, Clippy `--all-targets`, ESLint, tests, typos,
  cargo-deny, cargo-machete, gitleaks, shellcheck, audits, and both builds.
- Triage vulnerabilities immediately or document mitigation in the PR.
- If plans shift, update the relevant committed design or architecture docs. Keep
  `docs/superpowers/` and the root `plans/` directory local and untracked.

## Repository Hygiene

### Worktree lifecycle

- Create a worktree only when isolation is needed. Before creating one, inspect
  `git worktree list --porcelain` and record the task-owned path, branch and any
  dedicated build directory in ignored `tmp/` task notes. Treat pre-existing
  worktrees and unrelated changes as user-owned; never sweep them automatically.
- The coordinating session owns cleanup of every worktree it creates or delegates,
  including `.worktrees/` and `.claude/worktrees/agent-*`. Delegate completion does
  not transfer that responsibility. Before ending the task, stop task-owned
  processes and remove its worktrees, disposable branches and dedicated Cargo
  target directories, subject to the preservation rules below. Never delete a
  shared target directory or a directory whose ownership is uncertain.
- Before removal, preserve the work through either a verified merge into the
  intended integration branch under the existing PR/merge gates, or a local
  archive. For an archive, commit only task-owned outstanding changes (including
  intended untracked files), run the required commit checks, and create a unique
  `archive/<worktree-name>-<timestamp>` tag at the final branch tip. Verify the tag
  resolves to that tip and the worktree is clean before deleting anything. Never
  overwrite an existing archive tag, include secrets/ignored build output, or
  discard unrelated edits to make cleanup succeed. Cleanup does not authorize
  merging, pushing, bypassing review or running `entire clean`.
- Run removal from a surviving checkout with `git worktree remove <path>`, then
  `git branch -d <branch>` for a merged branch. Use `git branch -D <branch>` only
  for a task-owned archived branch after verifying its archive tag. Never use
  forced worktree removal, hard reset or bulk directory deletion to bypass a
  dirty worktree. Detached worktrees require the same preservation of their final
  commit before removal; there is no branch to delete.
- A pending PR, unresolved conflict, user decision, active concurrent session or
  failed preservation/cleanup step is an explicit retention exception. Preserve
  the required branch for an open PR; remove its clean worktree if no active work
  needs it. Recheck `git worktree list --porcelain` and task-owned branches/build
  paths before the final reply. Report cleanup performed and name every retained
  path/branch, its reason and the next action; never silently leave task worktrees.

- Keep implementation plans, research, investigation notes and scratch scripts
  under ignored `tmp/`; remove them when the work is complete.
- Merge durable decisions into the maintained owning guide. Do not commit
  completed-work reports, score histories, duplicate runbooks or archive copies.
- `docs/evals/` owns reusable suites/inventories, prompts and its README only.
  Generated evidence belongs in ignored output or PR/CI artifacts.
- Run `node scripts/check-repository-hygiene.mjs` before committing. The shared
  index check also runs in pre-commit, CI and health, rejecting ignored files
  even when force-added. See `docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md` for ownership.

- `crates/mesh-talk-integrations/` owns scoped local messaging grants, private IPC,
  and the dedicated bot host/admin CLI; `crates/mesh-talk-mcp/` adapts its four
  send/context/status tools to the official MCP SDK. Neither owns mesh crypto.
- Integration/e2e suites live in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` (`two_node_cli`,
  `persistent_history`, `post_office_offline`, `decoder_smoke`); keep unit tests inline via
  `mod tests` (e.g. `node/node_tests.rs`).
- React client sits in `frontend/src`; Vite tooling in `frontend/package.json`.
- Operational scripts in `scripts/` (`setup-hooks.sh`, `check-health.sh`); architecture in
  `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; conventions in `specifications/`. The
  [documentation map](docs/README.md) routes readers to maintained guides; the
  [documentation guidelines](docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md) define ownership
  across the README, guides, and project site.

## Build, Test, and Development Commands

- `make dev` primes Rust + Node deps and installs git hooks.
- `make build` / `make frontend-build` — release build / Vite production build.
- During feature development, preview changed-boundary validation with `make test-plan`
  and run it with `make test-changed`. Unmapped changes require an explicit owner
  and reason; inspect escalation notes for browser/native or consumer checks.
  Use `make verify-plan` / `make verify-changed` at task completion to compose the
  same affected tests with applicable formatting, lint/types and builds. The
  test-only commands do not include static checks; neither mode replaces required
  PR/review, browser/native or release gates. `make validation-report` separates
  queue and execution costs; `make validation-audit` compares a clean affected
  plan with same-source broader failure evidence before narrowing any gate.
  Read selected capability references and inspect pending browser/native requirements.
  Execution prints a structured feedback report; follow the
  [validation protocol](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#validation-stages-and-agent-responsibilities)
  for completed work, remaining evidence and additive semantic selections.
- During feature development, run affected tests only: `make test-focused
TEST_PACKAGE=mesh-talk-core TEST_FILTER=node::account_sync` selects Rust unit
  tests; add `TEST_TARGET=bridge_cross_lan` to select one integration target.
  `cd frontend && npm test -- src/features/chat/settingsDialogSession.test.ts`
  selects a frontend unit file. `make test` runs the full workspace suite
  (`cargo test --workspace`) for pre-PR and CI gates;
  `make e2e` runs the `#[ignore]`d multi-process backend rigs; `cd frontend && npm run e2e`
  runs the Playwright UI suite. Test builds use cheap KDF params (the `fast-test-kdf`
  feature), and `.cargo/config.toml` caps test/compile parallelism.
- UI / node spot checks: `make tauri-dev`, `make frontend-dev`,
  `cargo run -p mesh-talk-core --bin mesh-talk-node -- --keystore /tmp/a.keystore
--password pw --name alice` (add `--post-office` for relay mode).

## Coding Style & Naming Conventions

- Rust: `cargo fmt` (4-space, `snake_case` modules, `UpperCamelCase` types) +
  **`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`** (must match CI — `--all-targets` covers
  tests/benches).
- Frontend: `npm run format` (Prettier) + `npm run lint` (ESLint flat config).
- Write documentation and reusable prompts in English unless a specific exception is needed.
- Reference `specifications/development_conventions.md` for naming nuances.

## Domain Language

- `CONTEXT.md` is the canonical domain glossary. `docs/domain-design.md` indexes
  the modeling references and defines DDD vocabulary and naming translations.
- Distinguish local users, accounts and devices; desktop, transport and ratchet
  sessions; discovery, presence, custody, recipient delivery and read state.
- Use explicit identity/lifetime names in new code. Preserve public, wire and
  stored identifiers unless a separately validated compatibility change is intended.
- Update the glossary and affected owning guides when a domain meaning changes;
  link to definitions instead of maintaining duplicate glossaries.

## Architecture & Components

- Before adding business logic, consult [module ownership and reuse](docs/module-boundaries.md),
  inspect the owning module and its callers, and extend its existing implementation.
  Parallel tasks should name their owned paths and shared-interface dependencies;
  coordinate changes to shared interfaces through one integration owner. Keep
  feature-specific helpers local and share rules when their meaning and lifecycle
  are the same. The guide owns the detailed assignment and handoff contract.
- Stack: Rust 2024 on Tokio; Tauri 2 + React shell. No vendor-operated server.
- The `Node` (`node/node.rs`) wires identity + signed UDP **multicast** discovery
  (group `224.0.0.167`, port 47474) + Noise-encrypted TCP transport (`transport/`,
  low-level socket in `transport/net.rs`) + the content-addressed event log + DM/channel/
  file crypto. Messages are events synced as a bounded append-only log, account-addressed
  across a user's devices; optional offline custody via equal eligible post offices.
  Routed discovery and opt-in post-office federation connect reachable sites without
  joining their IP subnets. Wire formats are versioned bincode.
- See **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`** before changing crypto, sync, or transport;
  **`docs/network-design-reference.md`** owns the communication invariants,
  module contracts, resource budgets and topology acceptance boundaries.

## Maintaining standards as requirements change

- Before changing tests, fixtures, dependencies or workflows in ways that affect
  CI cost or reliability, read [CI maintenance](docs/ci-maintenance.md). Reuse
  existing owners, measure the affected cost, and preserve acceptance evidence;
  keep required-check policy in its existing owner.
- Before implementation, identify the existing decision owner, authoritative rule,
  observable acceptance criteria, affected consumers and required boundary evidence.
  Extend the owning implementation and `validation.json`; new business capabilities
  should link their guide and invariants. Explain an unchanged contract in the PR.
- Run `make standards-check` after adding/moving source or changing contracts. It
  checks structural ownership and maintained references, including new files; it
  does not prove assertion quality, semantic completeness or candidate readiness.
  Hooks inspect the working tree, so partially staged commits still need a clean
  committed-candidate check in CI. Frontend dependencies must be installed.
- When CI exposes a local omission or flaky fixture, fix the owning selector, task
  or fixture and add a focused regression. Review timing and selection evidence
  before changing policy. Follow the maintained
  [requirement maintenance loop](docs/testing-feedback-loop.md#maintaining-standards-across-requirements).

## Testing Guidelines

- Integration coverage in `crates/mesh-talk-core/tests/` and `node/node_tests.rs`; embed
  unit tests near the code. Networking/crypto changes ship a loopback integration assertion.
- Backend multi-process E2E via `make e2e` (CI: `e2e-backend.yml`); Playwright UI E2E via
  `cd frontend && npm run e2e` (CI: `e2e-ui.yml`).
- Do not run full suites or E2E automatically during ordinary feature work. Run
  the affected unit or integration tests as changes are made; run E2E and the
  comprehensive health gate on explicit request, for optional full local preparation,
  or in CI.
- See `docs/testing-feedback-loop.md` for selection examples and escalation triggers.
- Document executed validation commands in every PR; ensure `make test` passes
  locally or through its matching CI workspace suite before merge.

## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines

- Before changing product versions or release automation, read [the version lifecycle](docs/updates.md#version-ownership-and-lifecycle).
  Root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.package].version` is authoritative. Use
  `node scripts/release/version.mjs check|sync|prepare VERSION` (the `VERSION` argument belongs
  to `prepare` only); do not hand-edit generated npm/Cargo lock metadata or introduce another
  version constant. Root private npm metadata is a checked release-tooling projection;
  frontend private metadata is versionless and Tauri inherits Cargo. Never broadly replace
  matching dependency, fixture, history, wire or schema versions. Keep source builds `BASE-dev`,
  Nightlies `BASE-nightly.RUN.ATTEMPT`, official tagged builds `BASE`, and standard SemVer ordering.
- Version/changelog preparation and next-development-target changes use reviewed PRs. Ordinary main
  pushes must not create automatic release proposals or commit-derived product notes. Stable publication
  remains explicit through the existing verified tagged-release workflow; no direct main push,
  public empty release, mutable published tag or gate bypass. Nightly publication requires trusted
  `main` and a target above the latest Stable. Future changes must extend the existing version
  owner, its tests, standards/CI enforcement and capability contracts together; the owning guide
  documents permissions, bot-PR checks, dispatch and recovery requirements. Manual Stable draft
  preparation uses the reviewed exact-version CHANGELOG section and requires exact-source checks
  before creating its immutable tag/draft. The fixed release-history
  migration floor is historical provenance; never advance it during ordinary version bumps.

- Conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`); scopes like `feat(node):` align with
  `specifications/git_standards.md`. Squash WIP; link issues. When asked to merge,
  default to squash merge unless the user explicitly requests another strategy;
  follow the [merge policy](specifications/git_standards.md#pull-request-merge-strategy)
  and current-head required checks.
- Create PRs through `./scripts/create-pr.sh -- <gh pr create options>`.
  The default checks the clean committed candidate, comparison base, argument safety,
  whitespace, cheap affected static checks, ownership blockers, structural standards,
  repository hygiene and applicable verified frontend patch coverage before publication.
  Use `make pr-check` for the same cheap static phase; missing current coverage
  evidence reports its explicit generation command and never starts suites implicitly.
  Full cross-platform CI runs after publication; all required checks must pass on the
  current PR head before merging. Creating a PR does not certify test acceptance.
- To run comprehensive checks locally before publication, use
  `./scripts/create-pr.sh --full-preflight <selectors/specs> -- <gh pr create options>`.
  This invokes `prepare-pr.sh` (platform preflight plus full health). For an existing
  PR, `./scripts/prepare-pr.sh <selectors/specs>` provides the same optional local gate.
  Use Playwright specs relevant to changed frontend behavior and repeated
  `--core-filter` / `--host-filter` / `--integration-filter` / `--mcp-filter` selectors
  for changed Rust crates. Preflight runs selected tests in Linux Docker and through
  SSH to `windows10`; Windows workspaces, caches and temporary data stay on drive D.
  Owning scenario rules add visual specs and require real native evidence for
  lifecycle/discovery changes. Missing environments or empty Rust selections fail
  full preflight. Include `e2e/ui-visual-regression.spec.ts` for theme/layout changes.
  See `docs/testing-feedback-loop.md` for configuration, coverage and plan preview.
  Fetch `origin/main` first if the comparison base is stale.
- Record focused validation and outstanding checks in the PR. Use
  `./scripts/check-health.sh` when comprehensive local evidence is needed; protected
  CI remains required before merge regardless of local results.

## Security & Adjustments

- `./scripts/check-health.sh` chains fmt, Clippy `--all-targets`, ESLint, tests, typos,
  cargo-deny, cargo-machete, gitleaks, shellcheck, audits, and both builds.
- Triage vulnerabilities immediately or document mitigation in the PR.
- If plans shift, update the relevant committed design or architecture docs. Keep
  `docs/superpowers/` and the root `plans/` directory local and untracked.

## Repository Hygiene

### Worktree lifecycle

- Create a worktree only when isolation is needed. Before creating one, inspect
  `git worktree list --porcelain` and record the task-owned path, branch and any
  dedicated build directory in ignored `tmp/` task notes. Treat pre-existing
  worktrees and unrelated changes as user-owned; never sweep them automatically.
- The coordinating session owns cleanup of every worktree it creates or delegates,
  including `.worktrees/` and `.claude/worktrees/agent-*`. Delegate completion does
  not transfer that responsibility. Before ending the task, stop task-owned
  processes and remove its worktrees, disposable branches and dedicated Cargo
  target directories, subject to the preservation rules below. Never delete a
  shared target directory or a directory whose ownership is uncertain.
- Before removal, preserve the work through either a verified merge into the
  intended integration branch under the existing PR/merge gates, or a local
  archive. For an archive, commit only task-owned outstanding changes (including
  intended untracked files), run the required commit checks, and create a unique
  `archive/<worktree-name>-<timestamp>` tag at the final branch tip. Verify the tag
  resolves to that tip and the worktree is clean before deleting anything. Never
  overwrite an existing archive tag, include secrets/ignored build output, or
  discard unrelated edits to make cleanup succeed. Cleanup does not authorize
  merging, pushing, bypassing review or running `entire clean`.
- Run removal from a surviving checkout with `git worktree remove <path>`, then
  `git branch -d <branch>` for a merged branch. Use `git branch -D <branch>` only
  for a task-owned archived branch after verifying its archive tag. Never use
  forced worktree removal, hard reset or bulk directory deletion to bypass a
  dirty worktree. Detached worktrees require the same preservation of their final
  commit before removal; there is no branch to delete.
- A pending PR, unresolved conflict, user decision, active concurrent session or
  failed preservation/cleanup step is an explicit retention exception. Preserve
  the required branch for an open PR; remove its clean worktree if no active work
  needs it. Recheck `git worktree list --porcelain` and task-owned branches/build
  paths before the final reply. Report cleanup performed and name every retained
  path/branch, its reason and the next action; never silently leave task worktrees.

- Keep implementation plans, research, investigation notes and scratch scripts
  under ignored `tmp/`; remove them when the work is complete.
- Merge durable decisions into the maintained owning guide. Do not commit
  completed-work reports, score histories, duplicate runbooks or archive copies.
- `docs/evals/` owns reusable suites/inventories, prompts and its README only.
  Generated evidence belongs in ignored output or PR/CI artifacts.
- Run `node scripts/check-repository-hygiene.mjs` before committing. The shared
  index check also runs in pre-commit, CI and health, rejecting ignored files
  even when force-added. See `docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md` for ownership.

## Skills

### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/Users/kingsonwu/.codex/skills`

- `r4` = `/Users/kingsonwu/.codex/plugins/cache/openai-curated-remote/pages/0.1.26/skills`
